environments.L: local disposable PostgreSQL 18 cluster (initdb/pg_ctl present; committed fixtures allowed; no residue risk beyond the temp cluster)
environments.R: TEST Supabase, two concurrent psql sessions, ZERO-COMMIT rollback-only (no committed fixture may ever be relied upon)
environments.C: TEST Supabase, committed synthetic fixtures + explicit cleanup + residue proof - BLOCKED pending separate operator approval

namespaces.collision_rule: preflight aborts if ANY t6 id or key prefix is already present in any touched relation

isolation.rationale: the Worker/PostgREST path runs READ COMMITTED; the claim UPDATE race resolves by EvalPlanQual re-check after the row-lock wait (exactly-one-winner), whereas REPEATABLE READ would abort one session with 40001 and the fence/trigger post-wait reads would use a stale snapshot. T5's REPEATABLE READ was a single-session determinism device and must not be carried over.
isolation.deviation_from_t3_t5: documented and deliberate; the harness guard must assert read committed, not repeatable read

cases.title: two sessions claim the same pending request concurrently
cases.setup: committed fixture: one pending request, lease NULL
cases.pass: exactly one session receives the row; the other receives 0 rows; final attempt_count = initial+1 (never +2); exactly one distinct lease_token present; lease_expires_at within now()+5m +/- 2s
cases.blocked_or_fail: 0 or 2 winners, SQLSTATE 40001/55P03 anywhere, both sessions returning the same token, attempt_count +2

cases.title: expired-lease reclaim race
cases.setup: committed fixture: status deleting, lease_expires_at backdated 10m, attempt_count 2
cases.pass: exactly one winner; loser gets 0 rows; final attempt_count = 3; token replaced exactly once
cases.blocked_or_fail: two winners, 40001, attempt_count 4 or unchanged

cases.title: racing loser cannot transition state with its stale token
cases.setup: L01/L02 loser holds no lease; it attempts block_storage_deletion with the token it hoped for / the pre-race token
cases.sync: after L01/L02 completes, still inside loser session
cases.pass: block returns false (and fail/confirm return NULL/false as documented) AND a full-row before/after snapshot of the row is byte-identical
cases.blocked_or_fail: any state mutated by the stale token

cases.title: stale confirm after reclaim is rejected
cases.setup: A claims (token1); lease backdated; B claims (token2); A calls set_r2_confirmed_absent with token1
cases.pass: A's confirm returns false; row retains token2, r2_state unchanged by A; final row equals B's snapshot
cases.blocked_or_fail: A succeeds, row r2_state changed to confirmed_absent by stale worker

cases.title: two simultaneous batch claims partition the eligible set
cases.setup: 6 committed eligible pending requests in the t6 namespace
cases.pass: intersection of returned id sets is empty; every returned id was in the eligible set; no id returned twice across sessions; no error; claim completes below lock_timeout
cases.blocked_or_fail: any duplicate id, any ineligible id, any error; union size is INFO ONLY and is never required to equal 6 (timing-dependent)

cases.title: batch claim skips a row held by an open transaction
cases.setup: session A holds SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on eligible row X; 3 other eligible rows
cases.sync: A locks X, signals via pg_locks-visible state, then B batch-claims
cases.pass: B returns the other rows, does NOT return X, and completes without waiting (elapsed < lock_timeout); after A ROLLBACKs a follow-up claim returns X
cases.blocked_or_fail: B blocked until timeout, B returned X, or X permanently unclaimable

cases.title: blocked-backoff rows are not claimable under contention
cases.setup: 2 committed blocked rows (updated_at 30m ago), 1 blocked row (updated_at 2h ago)
cases.pass: both sessions return only the >=1h row's complement (i.e. the 30m rows never returned by anyone); the 2h row claimed exactly once across both sessions
cases.blocked_or_fail: a 30m-blocked row claimed, or the 2h row claimed twice

cases.title: second creator reuses the committed live request id (idempotent path)
cases.setup: A creates a request and COMMITs; B creates for the same key
cases.pass: B returns A's id; exactly one live row for the key after both
cases.blocked_or_fail: duplicate live rows, or B raises

cases.title: uncommitted creator serialises the competing creator on the per-key lock + live-key unique index
cases.setup: A begins and creates for key K (uncommitted); B creates for K with lock_timeout
cases.sync: B waits, A holds, then A ROLLBACKs
cases.pass: B blocks (wait observed in pg_locks), then after A's rollback B creates its own row successfully; exactly 1 live row; no error other than none
cases.blocked_or_fail: B raised a uniqueness/serialization error instead of waiting, deadlock 40P01, or two live rows

cases.title: claimer backend terminated after commit is reclaimable
cases.setup: A claims a committed row and COMMITs; A's backend is pg_terminate_backend'd
cases.pass: no lock remains for that row; B reclaims with attempt+1 and a new token
cases.blocked_or_fail: row stuck/unclaimable, orphan row lock, attempt not incremented

cases.title: claimer backend terminated mid-transaction leaves no state
cases.setup: A begins, claims (uncommitted), then is terminated
cases.pass: row is byte-identical to pre-race snapshot; B claims immediately and succeeds
cases.blocked_or_fail: any persisted lease/attempt from A's dead session

cases.title: opposite-order two-key lock attempts time out instead of deadlocking
cases.setup: A locks K1 then K2, B locks K2 then K1, both with lock_timeout=2s
cases.pass: zero SQLSTATE 40P01; at least one 55P03 lock_timeout observed; both sessions end in ROLLBACK with no held locks
cases.blocked_or_fail: any deadlock (40P01), any session left open, any lock retained
cases.note: production code paths take exactly ONE advisory lock per operation (static evidence), so this case only bounds the general risk

cases.title: documents reference INSERT waits for an in-flight fence, then succeeds after fence ROLLBACK
cases.setup: A (own txn): create own request for key K (self-visible), claim it, call fence_storage_key_for_deletion -> holds per-key advisory xact lock and an uncommitted fence row. B (own txn): INSERT documents row with storage_key K (own row).
cases.sync: state-based, in-database: A polls pg_locks joined to pg_stat_activity (application_name tags slmm-t6-a / slmm-t6-b) for B waiting on A's held advisory lock; B first polls for A's GRANTED advisory lock before issuing the INSERT; all polls bounded by statement_timeout
cases.pass: A observes exactly one waiter for its key lock; after A ROLLBACKs B's INSERT completes successfully (B sees no committed fence); both sessions end in ROLLBACK; T6-R08 residue clean
cases.blocked_or_fail: pg_locks/pg_stat_activity introspection unavailable (BLOCKED), B raised 23514 (implies a committed fence -> pre-existing residue, fail closed), B hit lock_timeout before A released (sync failure -> BLOCKED), any COMMIT

cases.title: same serialisation proven for a second source (payments.proof_key INSERT)
cases.setup: identical to R01 with payments fixture inserted by B
cases.pass: as R01; additionally B's insert row would have carried method constraints satisfied (use the corrected 'online' fixture value from b25555e)
cases.blocked_or_fail: as R01; also 23514 from payments_method_allowed indicates fixture drift -> BLOCKED (not a fence result)

cases.title: fence waits for an in-flight reference writer and re-checks freshly (returns fenced)
cases.setup: B (own txn) INSERTs documents row for key K and holds its transaction open (trigger holds the per-key lock). A (own txn) creates+claims its own request for K and calls fence -> blocks at the advisory lock. B polls pg_locks for A as waiter, then ROLLBACKs.
cases.sync: state-based: B detects A waiting; A never proceeds before B's rollback
cases.pass: waiter A observed by B; after B rollback A's fence returns 'fenced' (fresh post-wait snapshot under READ COMMITTED, per the documented behaviour at migration 20261017150000 lines 92-96); both sessions ROLLBACK; residue clean
cases.blocked_or_fail: A returned blocked_* (would mean a committed reference exists -> residue/fail closed), A never blocked (sync failure), any COMMIT

cases.title: lock_timeout produces a bounded, fail-closed wait (55P03), never an open-ended hang
cases.setup: A holds the per-key advisory xact lock (via its own fence on its own request); B sets lock_timeout='3s' and attempts the documents INSERT
cases.sync: B pre-waits for A's granted lock (state poll), then attempts
cases.pass: B fails with SQLSTATE 55P03 after ~3s (no 40P01), B's wrapper issues ROLLBACK, A observes the waiter then ROLLBACKs, residue clean
cases.blocked_or_fail: deadlock 40P01, wait longer than lock_timeout without error, session left open

cases.title: two sessions creating a request for the same fresh key serialise on the per-key advisory lock
cases.setup: A (authenticated identity for t6 owner) begins and calls request_storage_deletion(K) (own row uncommitted); B calls it for the same K
cases.sync: A polls pg_locks for B waiting; A ROLLBACKs; B completes
cases.pass: B's wait observed; after A's rollback B creates its own request (no committed duplicate exists); both ROLLBACK; residue clean
cases.blocked_or_fail: B raised before waiting, deadlock, any COMMIT, residue nonzero
cases.note: cross-session uniqueness/idempotency under COMMIT is L08a/L08b, not testable rollback-only

cases.title: zero-commit enforcement (statement allowlist)
cases.setup: runner inspects its own statement log for both sessions
cases.pass: no COMMIT statement ever issued in either session; only BEGIN/SET/SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DO/ROLLBACK present
cases.blocked_or_fail: any COMMIT anywhere -> immediate case-set FAIL + residue

cases.title: no open transactions or retained advisory locks after all R cases
cases.setup: read-only query after both sessions closed
cases.pass: zero pg_stat_activity backends with application_name LIKE 'slmm-t6-%'; zero backends with xact_start NOT NULL among them; consequently zero advisory locks attributable to T6
cases.blocked_or_fail: any surviving backend or lock -> FAIL, and operator runs recovery (idle_in_transaction_session_timeout / pg_terminate_backend as last resort, recorded)

cases.title: post-rollback zero-residue check over all relevant relations (separate READ ONLY session)
cases.setup: slmm-storage-deletion-t6-residue.sql: BEGIN ... READ ONLY; counts over the ten relations using t6 owner ids + key prefix, plus session/lock checks
cases.sync: runs last, after both sessions disconnected
cases.pass: all ten relation counts = 0 AND zero t6 backends AND zero t6-attributable advisory locks
cases.blocked_or_fail: any nonzero count -> fail-closed RAISE (never a PASS)

cases.title: L01 single-claim race repeated on TEST with committed fixture + cleanup
cases.pass: as L01 AND post-cleanup residue zero AND scheduler/cron confirmed inactive before and after
cases.blocked_or_fail: as L01, or cleanup leaves any row, or scheduler activity detected
cases.status: BLOCKED - requires separate approval to commit synthetic rows to TEST

cases.title: L05 batch disjointness repeated on TEST with committed fixtures + cleanup
cases.pass: as L05 AND cleanup residue zero
cases.blocked_or_fail: as L05

cases.title: committed fence rejects a cross-session reference insert (the rejection outcome untestable rollback-only)
cases.setup: A commits a fence for key K (via fence_storage_key_for_deletion on its own claim, then COMMIT); B INSERTs a documents reference for K -> must raise 23514 with the exact fence message; then cleanup: explicit DELETE of the fence row + request row, verified, then residue
cases.pass: B rejected with exact SQLSTATE 23514 + exact message 'Storage key is fenced for deletion.'; cleanup verified; residue zero
cases.blocked_or_fail: insert succeeded (fence not enforced cross-session), wrong error, cleanup incomplete
cases.status: BLOCKED - requires separate approval (committed fence row on TEST, even transiently)

rules: A case that was not executed is 'NOT RUN' - never PASS.
BLOCKED is a terminal recorded outcome with a reason, not a failure and not a pass.
Every R-case result must be echoed as a single JSON line from each session and captured to a file with SHA-256 recorded (fixes the T5 evidence gap).
ON_ERROR_STOP=1 in both sessions; any unexpected SQLSTATE aborts the case set and triggers the residue check.
The verdict block raises an exception when any expected PASS condition is unmet (mirrors the T5 raise-on-false contract).
